en: The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California.
Clay soil particles are smaller than 0.002 millimeters, making them much finer than sand particles which measure up to 2 millimeters.
Diamond is the hardest known natural mineral, scoring a perfect 10 on the Mohs scale, while the softest talc scores a 1.
About 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water, leaving only 3 percent as fresh water for drinking and farming.
Jupiter is so massive that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside its volume, making it the largest planet in our solar system.
The Sun is 150 million kilometers from Earth, but the next closest star, Proxima Centauri, is over 40 trillion kilometers away.
The Moon's diameter is about one-quarter that of Earth, and it orbits at an average distance of 384,400 kilometers from our planet.
A magnitude 7 earthquake releases about 32 times more energy than a magnitude 6 earthquake on the logarithmic Richter scale.
Mount Mayon in the Philippines has erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years, making it one of the most active volcanoes.
Super Typhoon Haiyan hit the Philippines in 2013 with maximum sustained winds of 315 kilometers per hour, making it one of the strongest tropical cyclones.
Saturn's rings span up to 282,000 kilometers wide, but they are extremely thin, measuring only about 10 meters thick in most places.
An average cumulus cloud contains about 500,000 kilograms of water droplets, which is roughly equal to the weight of five adult blue whales.
